Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

devote verb

give oneself or one’s time to

also devote oneself to, devoted to, be devoted to, give oneself up to, apply oneself to

classical

Cic. Q. fr. 3.5.4: sē litterīs (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 1.10: sē penitus mūsicīs (Lewis & Short)

dēdō, dēdere, dēdidī, dēditum

verb, third conjugation; sē dēdere + dative · Conjugation on Wiktionary

give up; with sē, devote oneself to

Cicero’s usual turn: sē litterīs, studiīs, alicui tōtum dēdere. The participle dēditus is “devoted to, given over to”. Its first sense is to give up, hand over, and of a city or army to surrender (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • incumbō, incumbere, incubuī, incubitum — throw oneself into, apply oneself to

    verb, third conjugation; in or ad + accusative, or dative · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.34: in aliquod studium (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Literally to lean or lie on something; of effort, to bend all one’s attention to a task (Lewis & Short).

  • operam dare (+ dative) — give one’s attention or effort to

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.11.1: operam dare, ut nē quid meōrum tibi esset ignōtum (Lewis & Short)

    The everyday phrase for spending one’s effort on something; with ut, to take care that.

  • dēvoveō, dēvovēre, dēvōvī, dēvōtum — vow to a god; devote to death

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Not the everyday word: chiefly to vow something to a god, or oneself to death for one’s country, as the Decii did; only rarely “devote oneself to” a person or cause (Caes. BG 3.22.2) (Lewis & Short).

  • sē dare (+ dative) — devote oneself to, give oneself up to

    also used · classical · Traupman 303

Examples

  • dēditī somnō cibōque

    given over to sleep and foodTac. Germ. 15.1

  • cui nōs tōtōs dēdere … dēbēmus

    to which (our country) we ought to devote ourselves entirelyCic. Leg. 2.5 (Lewis & Short)
